content_voiceover: This slide summarizes the twenty twenty-six NCCN guideline framework for early treatment response milestones in chronic myeloid leukemia, alongside the twenty twenty European LeukemiaNet criteria. Response is tracked using BCR-ABL1 international scale transcript levels at three, six, and twelve months, and color-coded into a red, orange, yellow, light green, and green scheme that guides clinical decision-making. A BCR-ABL1 level above ten percent at three months is yellow, signaling possible TKI resistance, but the same level persisting at six or twelve months turns red, indicating TKI-resistant disease. For red and yellow zones, clinicians should evaluate medication adherence and drug interactions, consider BCR-ABL1 kinase domain mutational analysis to detect resistance mutations, and consider bone marrow cytogenetic analysis for additional chromosomal abnormalities. The recommendation for red-zone disease is to switch to an alternate tyrosine kinase inhibitor other than imatinib and evaluate the patient for allogeneic transplant. A level between one and ten percent at three to six months is green, but becomes orange by twelve months if it hasn't dropped below one percent, again prompting consideration of a TKI switch or continuing therapy if complete cytogenetic response has been achieved. Levels between zero point one and one percent are green early on and light green by twelve months, reflecting TKI-sensitive disease where the treatment goal, whether long-term survival with a one percent target or treatment-free remission with a more stringent zero point one percent target, determines whether the current regimen continues or intensifies. A level at or below zero point one percent at any timepoint is green throughout, the ideal deep molecular response. The twenty twenty ELN table on the right mirrors this same logic with slightly different transcript thresholds and explicitly flags any BCR-ABL1 kinase domain mutation or high-risk additional chromosomal abnormality, such as an extra Philadelphia chromosome, isochromosome seventeen q, trisomy nineteen, monosomy seven or seven q minus, eleven q twenty-three rearrangement, or three q thirty-six point two, as automatically red regardless of transcript level.
keypoints: BCR-ABL1 international scale levels at 3, 6, and 12 months are color-coded from green to red to guide TKI management
Greater than 10 percent BCR-ABL1 at 3 months is yellow, but turns red if it persists at 6 to 12 months
Red or yellow zones prompt adherence review, kinase domain mutation testing, and consideration of a TKI switch
Deep response at or below 0.1 percent stays green and represents the treatment-free remission target
keypoint_voiceover: Remember the color logic. Green means stay the course, yellow and orange are early warning signs prompting adherence checks and mutation testing, and red means switch TKI and consider transplant. A BCR-ABL1 level above ten percent that hasn't improved by six months is the classic red flag, while getting down to zero point one percent or below is the deep molecular response needed for treatment-free remission.
